title: SLO alert thrash during blended multi-region failover due to hysteresis mismatch
creator: Emily Chen
description: During a blended failover test (canary + regional evacuation) we observed sustained SLO alert thrash and degraded tail latency for ~42 minutes. Multiple circuit breakers in the US-EAST and EU-WEST clusters opened and closed in rapid succession causing request replays, priority queue starvation, and repeated routing flips. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, mitigation steps taken during the event, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-18 09:05 UTC - Automated canary migration job (canary-rollout-5) started moving 3% traffic from US-EAST to EU-WEST
2026-02-18 09:07 UTC - Regional maintenance job triggered 'evacuate-shard' for US-EAST due to node remediation; routing weights updated incrementally
2026-02-18 09:09 UTC - First SLO alert: 99th pct latency > SLO for embeddings route in US-EAST
2026-02-18 09:12 UTC - Control-plane applied hysteresis policy A (30s) while edge-proxies still honoring policy B (8s) due to cached routing config TTL mismatch
2026-02-18 09:15 UTC - Circuit breakers in both regions oscillating; we saw repeated failover fallback to cheaper model variants which then saturated dedicated pools
2026-02-18 09:30 UTC - Oncall forced a staged rollback of the canary migration and temporarily disabled automatic region affinity rebalance
2026-02-18 09:32 UTC - Autoscaler reported headroom starvation in dedicated pools; token-bucket refill skewed across zones (refill timers misaligned)
2026-02-18 09:40 UTC - Traffic stabilized after manual intervention and adjusted hysteresis to 60s globally; alerts transitioned to recovery state by 09:52 UTC
impact: Outage window: 42 minutes of elevated tail latency leading to SLO alerts for three customer routes (text-generation, embeddings, chat). Visible user errors increased by ~0.6% for high-traffic tenants; internal dashboards showed 18% increase in request retries and 12% higher per-token cost during the event window.
root_cause: Multiple small failures combined: (1) configuration drift between control plane hysteresis and edge proxy TTLs caused inconsistent CB (circuit-breaker) state transitions; (2) the incremental routing weight propagation logic skipped an update to a subset of edge caches when maintenance and canary jobs overlapped; (3) token-bucket refill timers were misaligned after a scheduler upgrade, creating temporary headroom starvation in dedicated pools; (4) fallback routing policy allowed immediate downgrade to heavy-model variants without reserving burst capacity, amplifying pressure on KV cache warmup and priority queues.
mitigations_taken: Immediate: temporarily paused canary-rollout-5 and evict incremental routing job to force full config re-sync
Immediate: increased global hysteresis to 60s from mixed 8s/30s to stop oscillation
Immediate: applied emergency autoscaler scaling to reserve headroom and increased token-bucket refill alignment for affected zones
Short-term: enabled manual priority isolation for high-usage tenants to reduce starvation

ENG-231002: Fix routing propagation race — ensure incremental weight updater writes a propagation marker and retries on cache-miss (owner: Sara López, due: 2026-03-24)
ENG-231003: Audit token-bucket scheduler changes from 2026-02-10 upgrade and add automated timing-sanity tests (owner: Noah Kim, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-231004: Add canary/maintenance collision detector that blocks overlapping ops for the same shard (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-22)
ENG-231005: Create runbook 'slo-thrash-failover' with playbook steps and automated mitigations (owner: Oncall Team, due: 2026-03-12)
ENG-231006: Add a routing-config TTL mismatch monitor and dashboard tile with alerting (owner: Metrics Infra, due: 2026-03-20)
ENG-231007: Limit immediate fallback to heavy-model variants by reserving 10% burst capacity for graceful degrade (owner: Model Serving, due: 2026-03-30)
ENG-231008: Postmortem review with SRE, Runtime, and Routing teams to validate proposed fixes and confirm SLAs of changes (owner: Emily Chen, due: 2026-03-05)
follow_up_notes: We verified that the hysteresis TTL mismatch is reproducible in a staging harness; test-case attached to ENG-231002
Customer-facing postmortem draft prepared for Legal/Customer Success review — waiting on final metrics confirmation
There is a low-probability race still present if three ops (canary, maintenance, routing-update) overlap; the collision detector must be conservative
Consider adding a small randomized jitter to token-bucket refills to avoid alignment hazards across AZs
